title: Challenge: your first Kubernetes workload
intro: Deploy an app, watch Kubernetes keep it running, scale it, and expose it, the core kubectl loop every cluster operator uses daily. (Commands checked; output illustrative, no real cluster needed.)

steps.instruction: Create a Deployment named 'web' running the nginx image.
List the pods to see the one Kubernetes created for you.
steps.success:
NAME                   READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
web-6f9c8d7b5c-2xk9p   1/1     Running   0          8s

steps.instruction: Scale the deployment up to 3 replicas (for availability).
Expose the deployment as a Service on port 80 so other pods can reach it.
List the services to confirm 'web' got a stable ClusterIP.
steps.success:
NAME   TYPE        CLUSTER-IP      PORT(S)   AGE
web    ClusterIP   10.96.142.7     80/TCP    4s

done: Solved! create deployment → get pods → scale → expose → get svc. A Deployment keeps your pods running and replaces them when they die; a Service gives them one stable address. That's the heart of Kubernetes.
